title: Elementary sorts
learn: bubble, selection, insertion: how they work, O(n²), stability, when insertion sort wins (nearly sorted)
hook: "Walk me through insertion sort" and "which sorts are stable?" still come up in interviews, and knowing why these sorts are O(n²) is what makes O(n log n) sorts make sense.

explain.prompt: Explain how insertion sort works, its best and worst case, and when you'd actually choose it.
keyPoints: keeps a sorted prefix; each new element shifts larger ones right and drops into place
worst/average O(n²) (reverse-sorted input), best O(n) on already sorted input
good for tiny or nearly sorted arrays; Timsort uses it on small runs
